ai.description: This skink reaches 8 cm snout-vent length. It is bronze-brown with a pale dorsolateral stripe and four distinct keels on each dorsal scale. It features a dark lateral band and a white belly.
ai.identificationRemarks: The most reliable cue is the presence of exactly four distinct keels on the dorsal scales, which distinguishes it from other *Eutropis* species with more numerous keels.
ai.habitat: The Four-keeled Grass Skink inhabits moist deciduous forests and scrublands, typically found in leaf litter or near rocky outcrops at low to moderate elevations.
ai.behavior: The Four-keeled Grass Skink is primarily diurnal, actively foraging for small insects and invertebrates among leaf litter and low-lying vegetation during the day.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Eutropis quadricarinata* is oviparous, typically laying a clutch of 3–6 eggs. Breeding occurs during the pre-monsoon and monsoon months, from April to August in India.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Eutropis quadricarinata* is endemic to the Western Ghats of India, primarily inhabiting high-elevation evergreen forests and grasslands in Kerala and Tamil Nadu.
